title: Managing Cron Jobs 🛠️
description: List, edit, backup, and remove crontab entries. Understand system‑wide cron directories.

slides.title: Common Crontab Commands 🧾
slides.content:
## Beyond `-l` and `-e`

- `crontab -e` – edit the user's crontab.
- `crontab -l` – list jobs.
- `crontab -r` – remove the entire crontab (careful!).
- `crontab filename` – install a crontab from a file (overwrites existing).
- `crontab -u username -l` – view another user's crontab (requires root).

quizData.question: How do you delete all your cron jobs?
quizData.explanation: `-r` removes the crontab entirely. Editing and deleting lines also works, but `-r` is the nuclear option.

slides.title: Editing Tips ✍️
slides.content:
## Avoiding Mistakes

- Always backup: `crontab -l > backup`.
- After editing, list again to verify: `crontab -l`.
- Use comments (`#`) to document jobs.
- Set `MAILTO=""` to disable email (cron emails output to the user by default).
- Set `SHELL=/bin/bash` at the top if you need Bash‑specific features.

slides.title: A Well‑Organised Crontab
slides.codeSnippet:
SHELL=/bin/bash
MAILTO=admin@example.com
# Backup every night at 2:05 AM
5 2 * * * /opt/backup.sh
# Disk usage report every Monday at 9 AM
0 9 * * 1 /opt/report.sh

quizData.question: To disable email from cron, set the variable `___=""` in the crontab.
quizData.explanation: Setting `MAILTO=""` (empty string) prevents cron from sending mail.

slides.title: System‑Wide Cron Directories 📂
slides.content:
## The `/etc/cron.d`, `cron.daily` etc.

Besides user crontabs, there are system directories:
- `/etc/crontab` – system‑wide crontab (root only).
- `/etc/cron.d/` – extra system crontab files.
- `/etc/cron.hourly/`, `cron.daily/`, `cron.weekly/`, `cron.monthly/` – directories containing scripts run at those intervals (managed by `run-parts`).

You rarely need these unless you're a system admin.

slides.content: If you need root privileges for a cron job, use `sudo crontab -e` to edit the root user's crontab.
